causal_multiplier_summary: R_wall 1.843301x = F_plan 1.000000x [plan-shape, NUMERIC by node-by-node structural equality, not an A/B: both engines reach the same plan with no hint - parallel full scan of orders on the date range, then a first-match-exit probe into the FK B-tree on l_orderkey - with 573,671 index searches and 526,040 output rows identical on both engines and index entries agreeing to 0.18% (831,334 vs 832,822), the latter independently reproduced at 832,820 by a row_number() replay of the early-exit rule] x F_units 0.964986x [total-query-CPU/wall, U_P/U_C = 5.21484/5.40406 measured INSIDE the section 12 block, TWU 5.4391 vs 5.4209] x F_cpu 1.910185x [5.0075 vs 9.5652 core-s]. F_cpu = F_work 0.939713x [17,188,713 vs 18,291,452 tuple touches; 0.967541x once the node-decomposition artifact is collapsed, and the data-access counts agree to 0.18%] x F_cost 2.032732x [556.5 vs 273.8 ns per tuple touch]. Residual +0.000000%, and the report states plainly that this is an IDENTITY of the new instrument rather than a prediction: U is measured on the same block the headline is defined on and CPU_stmt = U x t_median. Closure rests on independent agreement instead - U vs the single-statement instrument (-1.8% CUBRID, +2.9% PostgreSQL), vs TWU (0.31% / 4.3%, the latter being the 0.235 s serial tail), vs perf task-clock (0.8%), and F_cpu reproduced to four decimals from perf as 1.9691x instructions per tuple x 1.0323x CPU-seconds per instruction at IPC 1.48 vs 1.51. Block-to-block reproducibility of R_wall is 1.826-1.859 over three independently gated blocks.
counter_direction_note: Reported in both directions: PostgreSQL wins by 1.8433x while spending 27.43% of its own query CPU (1.374 core-s) on per-statement parallel-worker page-table setup and teardown for the 8 GiB shared_buffers mapping - fault-in under ParallelWorkerMain->...->index_getnext_slot, teardown under __x64_sys_exit_group->exit_mmap->zap_pte_range - which CUBRID's threaded parallel-scan model does not pay at all. Net of that band F_cpu would be 2.63x rather than 1.91x. The campaign's dynamic_shared_memory_type=mmap contract is exonerated as the cause: live DSM segments are 32 KiB and 1 MiB and DSM symbols appear 4 times in 113,285 samples.

harness_defects_fixed: (1) harness/telemetry_run.py misfiled 0.68 core-s - 12.2% of total_query_cpu - from executor_cpu to auxiliary_query_cpu, because an exiting PostgreSQL child has an EMPTY /proc/<pid>/cmdline and fell through the cmdline test; total_query_cpu, TWU and U were unaffected but the SSOT section 15 split was wrong. (2) WARM was not established (above). (3) measure_block.sh aborted the attempt loop on a failed WARM gate instead of retrying. New harness/headline_telemetry.py closes Q03's carried-forward gap by sampling CPU inside the section 12 block; the old method would have left a -2.0065% residual. A suspected sampler perturbation was CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT rather than assumption: CUBRID's block wall is flat at 7.07-7.11 s across an 8x sweep of the sampling period, and the same sweep establishes that a period <= 0.1 s is required because coarser sampling misses PostgreSQL's transient per-statement workers (13.59 / 18.75 / 21.10 / 20.70 core-s at 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.05 s).

Ownership gates OK before and after every block; 34 engine TIDs at preflight and 35 after, 0 off-cpuset both times; CUBRID pool conserved at exactly 524,288 pages.
improvement_containment_note: IMP-002 and IMP-008 are disjoint profile bands, verified disjoint by symbol (kernel copy plus buffer manager versus predicate evaluation), and are NOT summed. IMP-002 and IMP-007 are two levers on the SAME core-seconds - miss count versus cost per miss - so adding them would double-count. Ranking on Q04: IMP-002 (25.5% of the CPU excess) > IMP-008 (18.1%) > IMP-007 (no asynchrony contrast on this query) > IMP-005 (zero runtime effect).

improvement_relations.IMP-002: existing Q01/Q03 candidate, Q04 relation added and priority RAISED P3 -> P1 - Q04's measured number refutes the former P3 justification that misses cost nothing material because device read_bytes is 0. At an identical 8192MB budget and an identical plan CUBRID misses 342,384 times per statement (10.45% of 3,277,822 fixes) and PostgreSQL misses 0 (3,013,495 accesses, read=0), costing 1.160 vs 0.000 core-s of kernel page-cache read/copy, call-graph verified to the pgbuf_fix_release miss branch and 25.5% of the CPU excess. Scope widened from repeated sequential scans to random index-driven access. PostgreSQL's working set is MEASURED to fit (830,217 of 1,048,576 buffers, 20.8% headroom); CUBRID's is PROJECTED at 8,510 MiB heap-only against 8,192 MiB from a model validated on the PostgreSQL side to 1.6 pp, with its index term UNMEASURED because db_index exposes no page count.
improvement_relations.IMP-005: existing Q03 candidate, Q04 relation added as a NEGATIVE CONTROL - under a 6-worker parallel scan every counter is exact (readrows 15,000,000 vs a true 15,000,000; readkeys 573,671 vs a true 573,671; lookup rows 526,040 vs a true 526,040), because Q04's XASL hangs the correlated EXISTS off the ROOT dptr_list and has no scan_ptr chain, so the duplicating loop at px_scan_trace_handler.cpp:493-500 never runs. This SCOPES the defect and pins the root-dptr path with exact numbers a fix must preserve; it does NOT clear the :496-499 inner dptr_list loop. A Q04 regression pin was added to its validation criteria.
improvement_relations.IMP-006: explicitly NOT related to Q04 - considered and rejected. The list-file materialization path runs, but this plan materializes only 526,040 result tuples rather than an intermediate join stream and fetch_val_list reaches just 0.55% of profile. No relation was recorded that the profile does not support.
improvement_relations.IMP-007: existing Q03 candidate, Q04 relation added but explicitly NARROWED - 276,950 blocking pread() calls per statement at exactly 16,377 bytes each versus PostgreSQL's 415 is the sharpest syscall evidence in the campaign, but on Q04 the io-worker asynchrony contrast that motivated the candidate does NOT apply, because PostgreSQL performs zero physical reads and so has nothing to overlap. The Q04 relation is annotated so it cannot be misread as evidence for asynchrony.
improvement_relations.IMP-008: P1 expression/type, measured, NEW - scan sargs route every row through the generic tp_value_compare_with_error() with per-call domain resolution (query_evaluator.c:2741 -> :1666 -> :2150 -> :152 -> :271/:276, object_domain.c:10404), where PostgreSQL compiles the qual once into type-specialized ExprEvalSteps (execExpr.c:229/:2789, execExprInterp.c:252/:719/:996, date.c:404/:431). 1.080 vs 0.255 core-s over 30,832,820 identical comparisons = 35.0 vs 8.3 ns each; 18.1% of the 4.558 core-s CPU excess.

measurement_protocol_note: Q04 changed how a headline block is measured, and the change altered the result. The first accepted blocks passed the physical-read half of the section 12 WARM proof but FAILED the steady-state half: PostgreSQL's three measured statements sat 2.1% above steady state (14 repeats settle at ~947 ms) and CUBRID's LEVEL was inherited from the preceding workload (first block median 1.706 s; every later block reproduces 1.774-1.779 s), because Q04's working set does not fit CUBRID's pool so residency is history-dependent. Section 12 says a failed WARM gate invalidates the run and restarts at warmup, so both first blocks were invalidated and re-measured through a new harness/warm_establish.py stage that proves convergence before timing. Uncaught, the headline ratio would have been 1.755x instead of 1.843x - a 4.8% error that would not have reproduced. The mandated regime still places PostgreSQL's measured statements +1.39% above its own long-run steady state versus CUBRID's -0.17%, so the contract headline UNDERSTATES CUBRID's deficit by ~1.5% against a steady-state ratio of 1.8720x; the contract number is the headline, and the bias is recorded rather than corrected.
